key_insight: The paper introduces quantum probabilistic local differential privacy, a relaxed privacy model that allows rare privacy violations and derives its structural properties and sample-complexity consequences for quantum hypothesis testing.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum ML and quantum information practitioners a more flexible privacy framework with concrete guarantees for designing private quantum protocols under realistic noise and resource constraints.
method: Defines quantum probabilistic local differential privacy via a low-probability spectral violation event.
Proves composition and unitary post-processing properties, while showing it is not generally convex or closed under arbitrary quantum channels.
Links the privacy notion to hockey-stick divergence and Neyman-Pearson testing to derive hypothesis-testing sample complexity bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytic results and derived bounds across representative depolarizing-noise scenarios, rather than experimental measurements.
watch_item: Because the privacy notion is not preserved under arbitrary post-processing and is not generally convex, implementations must carefully track allowed quantum operations.
paper_title: Quantum Probabilistic Local Differential Privacy: Structural Properties and Sample Complexity Bounds
